notes: Planned data-centre campus of up to 1,000 MW. No public commissioning schedule has been announced.
Planned data-centre campus of up to 1,000 MW in Skellefteå. Development depends on permitting.
SEK 95 billion investment framework enabling expansion from 300 MW to 750 MW. Full build-out is expected over a 10–15 year period.
Planned campus scale-up to around 600 MW. Full build-out is expected to occur gradually after 2027, but no firm commissioning year has been identified.
Planned 300 MW campus at Hamre Industrial Park. The 50-hectare site is prepared for high-density racks and is expected to enter operation in H1 2028.
First phase of the Strängnäs AI centre, corresponding to the original 300 MW plan before the later expansion to 750 MW. Exact construction and commissioning dates have not been publicly specified.
The facility is designed to expand to more than 300 MW within five years after the first phase. The value is treated as cumulative site capacity, not an incremental addition.
First phase of EcoDataCenter’s mega-campus at Kvarnsveden, with at least 250 MW of capacity. The first halls are planned to be completed in 2027.
Full build-out plan to scale the facility to 150 MW. No firm commissioning year for the full build-out has been identified.
Second phase planned for rapid expansion. Total cumulative capacity is expected to reach around 95 MW by 2026.

Memorandum of understanding to investigate a data centre at Studsvik supplied by small modular reactors (SMRs) of around 55 MW per reactor. Serial production of the reactors is expected no earlier than the early 2030s.
Planned metro data centre near SWE01. Expected to enter operation in Q4 2027 with 30 MW of capacity, including heat-recovery integration and a new customer substation.
Planned full build-out of more than 28 MW of IT capacity, corresponding to approximately 40 MW of power supply, by 2029. The entry reflects the developer’s broader Stockholm expansion plan.
Partnership to build an AI-focused data centre at the Borlänge campus. The facility is expected to open in 2027 with an estimated compute capacity of around 23 MW.
First phase with 20 MW of IT load, expected to be completed in 2026.
Initial 20 MW HPC phase at Marviken, expected to enter operation in 2025.
Flagship AI data centre with 16,000 GPU slots. Construction is planned to start in the first half of 2025, with operation in the second half of 2026.
First phase of the new Stockholm 5 project, with around 14 MW of IT capacity and 28 MW of power supply, planned to enter operation in June 2027.
Expansion adding 8 MW to Stockholm 4 South, increasing the facility from 20 MW to 28 MW. The additional capacity is expected to be available on 1 January 2026.
Data centre developed in a rock cavern. The first phase, up to 6 MW, is expected to be completed in Q4 2026.
Expansion of GlobalConnect’s existing data centre in southern Stockholm. Adds 1.2 MW of capacity, increasing the facility to 2.7 MW, with launch expected in 2026.

phase: Permitted backup power / no load estimate
notes: In 2021, the Land and Environment Court granted a permit for a data centre with up to 1,500 MW of installed backup-power capacity. Google has not made a final investment decision and must commence the permitted activity by 2031. The thermal capacity of the backup-power installation is not treated as IT load or grid load; no public load estimate has been identified.
